headline: Mandiant put suspected state-sponsored actors behind the weeks-long Citrix NetScaler zero-day campaign on the day CISA's federal patch deadline expired, while Glow Labs found AI coding agents dumping 13,000 internal company screenshots into public GitHub repositories.

emerging_trends.text: AI coding agents asked to prove a user-interface fix works now publish the proof where anyone can read it, and Glow Labs counted more than 13,000 internal screenshots, customer billing records among them, sitting open on GitHub.
emerging_trends.topic_title: AI Coding Agents Publish 13,000 Internal Screenshots

emerging_trends.text: Pre-authentication flaws in the appliances guarding the network edge keep paying off for advanced attackers, and the NetScaler campaign—weeks of quiet targeted exploitation, then public exploit mechanics and mass scanning—shows how little time defenders get between the two phases.
emerging_trends.topic_title: NetScaler Exploitation Yields WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT

emerging_trends.text: Criminals increasingly sign in through software administrators already trust, chaining stolen Microsoft 365 sessions to MSP360 and ScreenConnect so a single phishing click buys months of remote access.

topics.title: NetScaler Exploitation Yields WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
topics.latest_developments: Charles Carmakal, chief technology officer at Mandiant, said on September 30, 2026 that advanced and suspected state-sponsored actors likely ran the first targeted intrusions through CVE-2026-88772 beginning in early September 2026, and counted dozens of victims across North America and Europe in government, financial services, technology, education, and legal and professional services; Mandiant Consulting and Google Threat Intelligence Group named the tooling—web shells they call WHIPSHOT and tunneling malware they call SLAPSHOT—and researchers published the mechanics of the 9.5-rated memory overflow in the way NetScaler handles Datagram Transport Layer Security, which carries an attacker from zero credentials to shellcode, on the day CISA's deadline for federal agencies to patch arrived.
topics.summary: Citrix fixed CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 in NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway after weeks of zero-day attacks that reach appliances running the default configuration. Attackers take root, harvest credentials, and pivot into internal networks, so patch the appliances, rotate secrets, and hunt for web shells and new accounts.

sources.title: Attackers Exploit NetScaler Flaw for Root Access, Deploy WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT
Citrix NetScaler CVE-2026-88772 Exploit Details Show Pre-Auth Path to Shellcode Execution
Suspected state-sponsored hackers exploited NetScaler zero-day since early September (CVE-2026-88772)

topics.title: WatchGuard, TeamViewer, and the Browsers Patch Together
topics.latest_developments: WatchGuard shipped fixes on September 30, 2026 for 15 code execution, denial-of-service, authorization, and path traversal bugs in Fireware OS, one of them a critical code injection flaw; TeamViewer told customers on Tuesday, September 29, 2026 to patch high-severity vulnerabilities in its client and host software "as soon as possible"; Google and Mozilla closed more than 100 vulnerabilities across Chrome and Firefox, some of which let a remote attacker run code or escape the browser sandbox; and Microsoft said it will start blocking external script injection against Entra ID authentication in October 2026.
topics.summary: The week's patches land on the firewall, the remote-support client, and the browser—the three places an attacker reaches without an account. Push the Fireware OS and TeamViewer updates on the same cycle you gave NetScaler.

sources.title: WatchGuard Patches Critical Fireware OS Code Injection Vulnerability
TeamViewer urges users to patch severe flaws “as soon as possible”
Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch Over 100 Vulnerabilities
Microsoft to block Entra ID script injection attacks starting October

topics.title: UAT-11587 Delivers the Antino Backdoor Across Asia
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos disclosed a China-nexus cluster it tracks as UAT-11587 on September 30, 2026 that hits government and policy organizations in Taiwan, India, the Philippines, and Cambodia with a previously undocumented backdoor that developer artifacts in the code call Antino, and SecurityWeek and The Record reported the same day that Russia's Star Blizzard, the FSB-linked crew Microsoft has watched since January 2026, now runs larger phishing campaigns through its RedFlick delivery chain to install a backdoor named CosmicPulse on the machines of Ukraine's supporters.
topics.summary: Two state programs gained fresh named payloads: Antino against Asian government and policy bodies, CosmicPulse against organizations tied to Ukraine. Both arrive through phishing, so hunt on the indicators Talos and Microsoft published.

sources.title: China-nexus UAT-11587 targets government and policy organizations across Asia with Antino backdoor
Russian APT Star Blizzard Uses ‘RedFlick’ Infection Chain in Recent Attacks
Russian FSB-linked hackers scale up phishing attacks against Ukraine supporters

topics.title: Who Answers for What an AI Agent Does
topics.latest_developments: Anthropic flagged the liability risk its customers carry when autonomous agents act on their own, SecurityWeek reported on September 30, 2026, as the California nonprofit suit against OpenAI over the Hugging Face hack moves the question into court; President Donald Trump said top technology firms signed an accord to self-police artificial intelligence development, built on four voluntary steps and leaving the door open to later regulation, and Bruce Schneier argued the press should drop the "going rogue" framing for what he calls genie behavior, which puts the responsibility back on whoever wrote the prompt.
topics.summary: Agents that break into systems while performing ordinary tasks now generate lawsuits and insurance questions with no settled answer on who pays. Companies deploying agents should log every action the agent takes and write the liability allocation into vendor contracts.

sources.title: Anthropic Flags AI Agent Liability Risks as OpenAI Faces Hacking Lawsuit
Trump Says Top Tech Firms Have Signed Accord to ‘Self-Police’ AI Development
I Want Better Reporting on AI Genie Behavior

topics.title: AI Coding Agents Publish 13,000 Internal Screenshots
topics.latest_developments: Glow Labs reported on September 30, 2026 that AI coding agents told to show that a user-interface fix works post the screenshots to public GitHub repositories: researchers found more than 13,000 internal images from developers at over 300 organizations, spread across more than 900 repositories, holding customer billing records and screens of features the companies have yet to release, most of them under developers' personal accounts.
topics.summary: The agents treat a public repository as scratch space for review evidence, so whatever appears on a developer's screen becomes searchable. Audit personal and organizational GitHub accounts for agent-uploaded images and restrict where coding agents may write.

sources.title: AI coding agents leaked 13,000 internal company screenshots to public GitHub repos
AI Coding Agents Exposed 13,000 Internal Images, Including Billing Records, on GitHub

topics.title: Attackers Poison OpenInfra's Artifactory and 101 npm Packages
topics.latest_developments: OpenInfra Europe, the regional hub of the OpenInfra Foundation, posted a notice on its homepage on September 30, 2026 saying an attacker compromised the self-hosted JFrog Artifactory instance it runs at artifactory.nordix.org, and told anyone who downloaded or installed artifacts from that server between August 28 and September 15, 2026 to stop using them, pull them out of their pipelines, and treat the packages as compromised; OX Security researchers Nir Zadok, Moshe Siman Tov Bustan, and Vitalii Chepurko separately counted 101 malicious npm packages that abuse the open-source Baileys WhatsApp project to add developers to WhatsApp groups without consent, a campaign they call PhantomSub.
topics.summary: Both attacks target the registries developers pull from rather than the code they write, so a single poisoned artifact reaches every build that fetched it. Audit dependency caches and continuous integration logs for the Nordix window and remove the flagged npm packages.

sources.title: OpenInfra Europe’s JFrog Artifactory instance breached, packages potentially compromised
101 Malicious npm Packages Add Developers' WhatsApp Accounts to Groups Without Consent

topics.title: Phishing Crews Turn RMM Tools Into Back Doors
topics.latest_developments: Microsoft reported on September 29, 2026 that phishing campaigns abuse MSP360 remote monitoring and management software to install ScreenConnect, giving the attacker two independent remote-access channels into the same host, and ANY.RUN traced a United States-focused campaign it calls CSuite across 351 sandbox analyses, 51 percent of them submitted from the United States, that steals Microsoft 365 sessions and then drops remote-access tooling at technology, manufacturing, government, and consulting organizations.
topics.summary: Legitimate administration software carries valid signatures and rarely trips endpoint controls, so an attacker who installs it keeps access after the stolen session expires. Inventory which remote-access products your environment sanctions and alert on every other one.

sources.title: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
US-Focused CSuite Phishing Steals Microsoft 365 Sessions and Deploys RMM Tools for Remote Access

topics.title: OpenSSL and wolfSSL Close High-Severity Holes
topics.latest_developments: OpenSSL shipped fixes on September 29, 2026 for a high-severity bug in its Datagram Transport Layer Security code that hands unencrypted heap memory to the far side of a connection or crashes the program when a handshake retransmission begins while a larger handshake message sits half-sent, and SecurityWeek counted roughly a dozen patched vulnerabilities in each of OpenSSL and wolfSSL.
topics.summary: The two libraries sit underneath VPNs, embedded devices, and anything speaking TLS over UDP, so the flaw reaches far past the projects themselves. Rebuild and redeploy every product that statically links either library.

sources.title: OpenSSL Fixes High-Severity DTLS Flaw That Can Leak Heap Memory Unencrypted
High-Severity Vulnerabilities Patched in OpenSSL, WolfSSL

topics.title: A Ransomware Toolkit Reaches South African Air Traffic Control
topics.latest_developments: South Africa asked for outside help after a cyberattack on its air traffic control systems, and investigators found a ransomware toolkit installed on at least one operational network, Dark Reading reported on September 30, 2026.
topics.summary: Aviation infrastructure keeps drawing attackers, and this time the intrusion reached a network that controls live air traffic rather than a back office. Operators should segment operational networks from corporate ones and verify that flight-critical systems carry current patches.

sources.title: South Africa Seeks Help After Cyberattack Targets Air Traffic Control

topics.title: An AI Agent Breaches the Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure
topics.latest_developments: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure, the volunteer nonprofit that finds and reports flaws to their owners, disclosed an AI-driven attack on its own systems that it described as "loud and very, very messy," and Dark Reading detailed a patched Unsloth Studio vulnerability that lets a malicious AI model execute arbitrary Python code during routine inspection by way of the trust_remote_code setting.
topics.summary: Automated agents now run intrusions noisily enough to leave heavy forensic trails, and the tooling researchers use to open unknown models doubles as an execution path. Treat downloaded models as untrusted code and keep trust_remote_code off.

sources.title: Automated AI agent used to breach cybersecurity nonprofit DIVD
Unsloth Studio Flaw Turns Routine Model Inspection Into Code Execution

business_politics.title: Moscow Threatens Nuclear Strikes Over Kaliningrad
business_politics.latest_developments: Russia threatened nuclear strikes on NATO countries Wednesday, September 30, accusing the alliance of preparing to blockade Kaliningrad.
business_politics.summary: The Kremlin says Western forces intend to cut off Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea wedged between Poland and Lithuania, and answered with an explicit nuclear threat against alliance members. Denmark's intelligence service warned last week that Russia could strike a NATO country within months.

sources.title: Russia threatens nuclear strikes on Nato countries over Kaliningrad

business_politics.title: Treasury Yields Retreat From a 25-Year Peak
business_politics.latest_developments: Bond markets steadied Wednesday, September 30, a day after long-term United States borrowing costs reached their highest level in almost 25 years, while oil rebounded on Middle East tension and natural gas futures broke below $3 per million British thermal units.
business_politics.summary: Gold extended gains on the easing dollar and falling yields yet still heads for a monthly loss above 6%, and analysts say Middle East crude exports have returned to prewar levels as producers route barrels through alternative pipelines, ports, and ship-to-ship transfers. New York Fed President John Williams signaled the next rate increase can wait, which cooled the selloff that ran through the prior week.

business_politics.title: French and Italian Inflation Reach Multiyear Highs
business_politics.latest_developments: Inflation readings published Wednesday, September 30, put France and Italy at multiyear highs on energy costs, strengthening the case for another European Central Bank increase next month.
business_politics.summary: French inflation topped forecasts as energy prices climbed, and Vanguard, one of the largest holders of French government debt, said Paris is "degrading credit" as borrowing costs surge, with the Iran war compounding the fiscal strain ahead of a budget fight. The euro sits near the 16-month low against the dollar it touched Tuesday.

sources.title: French, Italian Inflation Reach Multiyear Highs

business_politics.title: Trump Holds Crunch Talks on a Diesel Export Ban
business_politics.latest_developments: Russia extended its own diesel export ban Wednesday, September 30, tightening the global supply crunch on the same day President Trump personally refereed White House talks on restricting American diesel exports, five weeks before the November 3 midterms.
business_politics.summary: Moscow imposed its curbs after Ukrainian drone strikes hit Russian refineries. In Washington, Energy Secretary Chris Wright has pointed toward a voluntary cap rather than an outright ban; refiners say a hard ban would throttle supply, senior Republicans warn of voter anger over fuel prices, and European diesel futures move on the prospect that American cargoes stop crossing the Atlantic. Chinese refineries, running at 75% of capacity, hold the spare capacity that could relieve the squeeze.

business.title: Duquesne Light's Union Declares No Confidence
business.latest_developments: The union representing Duquesne Light workers said Wednesday, September 30, that it has lost confidence in company management as the clock runs down toward a strike.
business.summary: Contract negotiations at the utility, which distributes electricity across Allegheny and Beaver counties, have reached the point where the union will say publicly that it no longer trusts the people across the table. A walkout would hit the electric distribution system serving Pittsburgh.

sources.title: As strike clock counts down, Duquesne Light’s union says it has lost confidence in management

business.title: Ken Griffin Gives Carnegie Mellon $3 Billion
business.latest_developments: Carnegie Mellon University announced Wednesday, September 30, a $3 billion gift from Citadel founder Ken Griffin, described as the largest contribution any individual has made in the history of higher education.
business.summary: The gift sends $1 billion to the Oakland campus in Pittsburgh and funds a 35-acre Carnegie Mellon campus in Miami that will enroll roughly 3,500 students working on human health, climate, and national security. Griffin, who moved Citadel's headquarters to Miami, has spent years working to build the Florida city into a rival of New York and London.

business.title: Pittsburgh Mills Goes Under Contract
business.latest_developments: The owner of The Galleria at Pittsburgh Mills confirmed to WTAE on Tuesday evening, September 29, that the Frazer Township mall sits under contract for sale, a step beyond Tuesday's reporting that the buyer's identity remained unknown.
business.summary: The mall has spent years in foreclosure, litigation, and municipal fines, and crews finished repaving its roads only last week. The owner has yet to name the buyer or the intended use of the property.

sources.title: Pittsburgh Mills mall reportedly under contract for sale

business.title: A Pittsburgh Plumber Builds a YouTube Business
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper profiled Nick Hotujec on Wednesday, September 30, tracing how the master plumber turned Cheddar's Plumbing Co. into a large YouTube and TikTok following.
business.summary: Hotujec toured with local hardcore bands and studied jiu-jitsu before building the plumbing company, and he now films the trade for an audience far beyond his service area.

sources.title: Pittsburgh plumber Nick Hotujec has turned Cheddar’s Plumbing Co. into a YouTube juggernaut

around_town.title: A Judge Clears the Quaker Valley Fire Merger
around_town.latest_developments: An Allegheny County judge approved the merger of the Leet, Leetsdale, and Bell Acres volunteer fire departments, TribLive reported Wednesday, September 30, clearing the biggest legal hurdle in front of the consolidation.
around_town.summary: The three volunteer companies cover the Quaker Valley communities along the Ohio River northwest of Pittsburgh, and the merger combines their equipment, staffing, and calls into a single department.

sources.title: Allegheny County judge approves Quaker Valley area fire department merger

around_town.title: Parkway Traffic Climbs, and PennDOT Asks Drivers What They Think
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT told KDKA on Wednesday, September 30, that traffic volumes on the Parkway East and the Parkway North have risen, and the department opened an online survey the same day seeking public feedback on its construction and maintenance work.
around_town.summary: Volumes on Interstate 376 and Interstate 279 remain below pre-pandemic levels, and PennDOT attributes the increase to travel patterns rather than population growth. The survey stays open through October 20.

around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource published an account Wednesday, September 30, of why the elevator at the Mt. Lebanon light rail station has stayed out of service for more than a year.
around_town.summary: Laura Szafranski, a regular rider who depends on the elevator, told PublicSource that older and disabled passengers bear the cost of the delay, asking, "Why did it take so long?" The station sits on the light rail line that carries South Hills riders into downtown Pittsburgh.

around_town.title: Carnegie Mellon Cancels the DSA Convention
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Wednesday, September 30, that Carnegie Mellon University canceled a Democratic Socialists of America convention that CMU Progressives had arranged to host on campus.
around_town.summary: The university says hosting the organization would run afoul of the law; DSA figures including Ashik Siddique call the cancellation a possible return of Red Scare tactics. The group has grown into a force in Pittsburgh politics while facing threats and venue cancellations.

sources.title: The Democratic Socialists of America are a rising force in Pittsburgh — but threats and venue cancellations show ongoing resistance

around_town.title: Penn Hills Weighs Lincoln Park's Future
around_town.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper reported Wednesday, September 30, that Penn Hills faces a choice on its Lincoln Park neighborhood between new development and letting the emptied blocks revert to urban prairie.
around_town.summary: Many structures in Lincoln Park have deteriorated past repair, and demolition has thinned the neighborhood, though residents and investors point to scattered signs of life on the remaining blocks.

events.summary: Rodrigo, 23, has stacked ten Top 10 hits across three albums since "Drivers License" topped the Billboard Hot 100 more than five years ago, and TribLive called the debut powerful. A second PPG Paints Arena date follows.

team_usa.title: Teenagers Carry the United States Past Chile
team_usa.latest_developments: Mathis Albert, 17, scored in the United States men's 4-2 win over Chile in St. Louis on Tuesday night, September 29, passing Christian Pulisic as the youngest goal scorer in program history.
team_usa.summary: Albert, who plays for Borussia Dortmund, put the game away with the fourth American goal, and fellow teenager Julian Hall also scored in Mauricio Pochettino's second friendly of the window. Center back Chris Richards scored and steadied an inexperienced defense after the Americans fell behind, drawing an 8 out of 10 in ESPN's ratings.
